entry.title: Agios Nikitas Beach, Lefkada
entry.summary: Agios Nikitas is a small village on the north-west coast of Lefkada, with a beach of pebbles and clear turquoise water. The village has no traffic in the centre, and a path leads to a second pebble beach called Milos. Steep hills with olive trees and pines surround the bay.

entry.title: Vasiliki Beach, Lefkada
entry.summary: Vasiliki is a village at the head of a long bay on the south of Lefkada, famous as one of the best windsurfing spots in Greece. The beach is made of fine pebbles, and the wind rises in the afternoon. Boats leave the harbour for the beaches of the west coast and for the islands.

entry.title: Nikiana Beach, Lefkada
entry.summary: Nikiana is a small seaside village on the east coast of Lefkada, with a long beach of pebbles, calm water and a view of the mainland hills. The beach is quieter than the famous beaches on the west coast. Tavernas stand along the promenade, and the water is warm in summer.

entry.title: Damouchari Beach, Pelion
entry.summary: Damouchari is a small bay on the Pelion peninsula, with a beach of pebbles, a few old stone houses and a tiny harbour. Dense green hills drop to the water, and the sea is clear and calm. The bay was used as a film location, and only a few tavernas stand at the shore.

entry.title: Plage de Valras, Herault
entry.summary: Valras-Plage is a seaside resort on the Herault coast, close to Beziers, with a long beach of fine sand and shallow water. A promenade and cafes line the shore, and the Orb river runs into the sea at one end. The beach is popular with families and is lively in summer.

entry.title: Plage du Barcares, Pyrenees-Orientales
entry.summary: Le Barcares is a seaside resort near Perpignan with a very long, wide beach of fine sand and a gentle slope into the sea. A lagoon lies behind the town, and the Pyrenees can be seen on clear days. The beach is popular with families and sailing clubs.

entry.title: Plage de La Ciotat, Provence
entry.summary: La Ciotat is a Mediterranean harbour town between Marseille and Toulon, with a long beach of sand and a gentle slope into the sea. The beach is known as one of the few sandy beaches in the area, and the old port and the cliffs of the Bec de l Aigle are close by. Rocky coves lie along the coast on either side.

entry.title: Plage d Arcachon, Gironde
entry.summary: Arcachon is a seaside town on the bay of the same name in south-west France, with a long promenade and a sandy beach along the shore. The water inside the bay is calm, shallow and sheltered from the Atlantic waves. Oyster huts and the Dune du Pilat lie a short distance away.

entry.title: Plage des Minimes, La Rochelle
entry.summary: The Plage des Minimes is a sandy beach beside the large marina of La Rochelle on the Atlantic coast. The tide goes out far and leaves a wide strip of sand. The beach is a short bike ride from the old harbour, and boats from the marina fill the view.

entry.title: Plage de Gruissan, Occitanie
entry.summary: Gruissan Plage is a long beach of fine sand on the Mediterranean coast of Aude, known for its colourful wooden stilt houses behind the shore. Winds from the land make it a favourite with kitesurfers and windsurfers. A lagoon, salt pans and a hill with a ruined tower lie close by.

entry.title: Bonassola Beach, Liguria
entry.summary: Bonassola is a small seaside village on the Ligurian coast, a short drive from the Cinque Terre, with a beach of pebbles and coarse sand. The water is clear, and the promenade and the old fishing houses make a pleasant walk. The village is quieter than its famous neighbours.

entry.title: Ansedonia Beach, Tuscany
entry.summary: Ansedonia is a wide sandy beach in southern Tuscany, below a hill with the ruins of the Roman town of Cosa. Dunes, pines and a lagoon lie behind the shore, and the water is clear and shallow at the edges. Beach clubs and free sections share the shore.

entry.title: Serapo Beach, Gaeta
entry.summary: Serapo is a long beach of golden sand below the old town of Gaeta in southern Lazio, with a gentle slope into the sea. A promenade and beach clubs run along the shore, and a cliff with a sanctuary rises behind the bay at one end.

entry.title: Fornillo Beach, Positano
entry.summary: Fornillo is a pebble beach on the Amalfi Coast, reached on foot from the centre of Positano along a short path. It is quieter than the main Marina Grande beach, with the pastel houses of the town above the shore and small boats on the water.

entry.title: Methoni Beach, Messinia
entry.summary: Methoni has a wide sandy beach beside a large Venetian castle on the south-west coast of the Peloponnese. The sea is shallow and clear, and the village has tavernas and rooms close to the shore. The castle can be visited in the morning or at sunset.

entry.title: Vlychada Beach, Santorini
entry.summary: Vlychada is a quiet beach on the south coast of Santorini, with dark volcanic sand and pebbles below pale eroded cliffs. A small harbour with tavernas sits at one end. The cliffs give the shore an unusual shape, and the beach is quieter than Perissa and Kamari.

entry.title: Finikounda Beach, Messinia
entry.summary: Finikounda is a village on the south-west coast of the Peloponnese, with a long beach of fine sand and a sea that is calm in the morning. Winds in the afternoon make it a popular spot for windsurfing and kitesurfing. Tavernas stand along the shore.

entry.title: Kalathas Beach, Chania
entry.summary: Kalathas is a sandy bay on the Akrotiri peninsula near Chania in Crete, with shallow turquoise water and bare hills around the shore. The water is calm and clear, and the beach is popular for sunsets. A few tavernas and rooms stand behind the sand.

entry.title: Praia de Caminha, Minho
entry.summary: Praia de Caminha lies at the mouth of the Minho river on the northern coast of Portugal, facing Spain across the water. The beach is wide and sandy, with calm shallow water near the river and Atlantic waves on the open side. The old town of Caminha is a short walk away.

entry.title: Playa de Isla Canela, Huelva
entry.summary: Isla Canela is a long beach of fine golden sand near Ayamonte on the Andalusian coast, close to the border with Portugal. Dunes and marshes lie behind the shore, and the water is shallow and warm in summer. The beach is quiet outside the main season.

entry.title: Playa de Castelldefels, Barcelona
entry.summary: Castelldefels is one of the longest sandy beaches near Barcelona, with a wide strip of golden sand and a seafront of beach bars. It is reached by a short train ride from the city, and in summer it is busy with families and surfers on windy days.

entry.title: Playa de Sotogrande, Cadiz
entry.summary: Sotogrande is a planned seaside resort in San Roque on the Andalusian coast, with a wide sandy beach, a marina and golf courses nearby. The beach is quiet outside the summer season, and on a clear day the coast of Morocco and the Rock of Gibraltar can be seen from the shore.

entry.title: Playa de Mazagon, Huelva
entry.summary: Playa de Mazagon is a long beach of fine golden sand on the Atlantic coast of Huelva, backed by cliffs and a pine forest. It lies inside the Donana area and is quieter than the busy resorts to the east. The water is Atlantic and the beach is wide at low tide.

entry.title: Armier Bay, Malta
entry.summary: Armier Bay is a sandy bay in the north-west of Malta near Mellieha, with shallow water and a view of the island of Comino across the channel. A row of small holiday houses sits behind the beach, and the sea is calm in summer. The beach is popular with local families.

entry.title: Xerokambos Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Xerokambos is a remote beach on the south-east coast of Crete, with pale sand, clear turquoise water and bare hills behind the shore. The area is far from the main resorts, and a few small hotels and tavernas serve the bay. Small rocky coves lie along the coast on either side.

entry.title: Follonica Beach, Tuscany
entry.summary: Follonica is a seaside town in the Maremma on the coast of southern Tuscany, with a long beach of fine sand that slopes gently into the sea. Pine woods and a promenade lie behind the sand, and the town is a classic Italian family resort. The island of Elba is visible across the water.

entry.title: Campese Beach, Giglio Island
entry.summary: Campese is the main sandy beach of the island of Giglio in the Tuscan Archipelago, with a small village and a medieval watchtower behind the bay. The water is clear and the bay is sheltered from some winds. Ferries link the island to the mainland port of Porto Santo Stefano.

entry.title: Baratti Beach, Tuscany
entry.summary: Baratti is a calm crescent bay of fine pale sand near Piombino on the Tuscan coast, with pine trees behind the shore and the island of Elba visible on a clear day. Etruscan tombs and an archaeological park lie close to the beach. The water is shallow and clear.

entry.title: Plage de Ouistreham, Normandy
entry.summary: Ouistreham is a seaside town at the mouth of the Orne river, with a long beach of fine sand and a seafront promenade. The ferry port for Caen and the Sword Beach landing site of June 1944 are close by. The tide goes out far and leaves a wide beach.

entry.title: Plage de Saint-Aubin-sur-Mer, Normandy
entry.summary: Saint-Aubin-sur-Mer is a seaside village on the Normandy coast, with a wide beach of fine sand and a long promenade. The beach was part of the Juno landing area in June 1944, and memorials stand near the shore. The tide goes out far and the sea is cool.
